_readme: Hand-written additions merged on top of the extracted rules data at load time.
Use this for content the upstream data is missing — most notably the class-specific
talent trees it references but never defines (Dark Side Devotee, Force Adept, Force Item,
Sith, Expert Pilot, Gunner, Knight's Resolve, Piracy, Military Tactics).
Add the talent itself under `features`, then list its id under the tree in `talentTrees`.
A tree stops being marked incomplete as soon as it has at least one talent.
Nothing here is validated against the books — it is whatever you type.
Icons: drop a file in public/icons/features/ (or classes/, weapons/) and name it here:
Only listed icons are rendered, so a missing file can never show as a broken image.
provenance: feature "superior-tech": requirements.levle -> requirements.level (prereq was never enforced)
49 species prerequisites retargeted from features -> species

Force Adept, Force Disciple and Sith Lord pointed at talent trees the source data never defined, while the trees they need sat unused under other names; those three were remapped. Without it those classes had no selectable talents at all.
12 Combined Feat rows hidden and rewritten as 8 entries in combos.json — they are automatic benefits, not selectable feats, and two of the eight had no row at all; see the note on them below
feature "attack-combo-fire-strike": a second copy of Attack Combo (Fire and Strike) under an "&" spelling; the stub is hidden and Soldier's bonus feats repointed at the full entry
_comment_lightsaber_chain: Saga Edition has two separate chains. The Elite Trooper one in Weapon Master chooses a
weapon group and is correct as imported — nothing here touches it. The Jedi Knight one in
Duelist is lightsaber-only: Greater Weapon Specialization (lightsabers), CR p.218, whose
prerequisites are the other lightsaber talents and nothing else.
The import gave the Duelist entry the Elite Trooper talent's content: the name lost its
(lightsabers), the description was the generic 'choose a weapon group' text, specType made
it ask which group, and the prerequisites pointed at the generic ids, which the Jedi path
never grants. So a Jedi 7 / Jedi Knight 5 holding the whole lightsaber chain was told it
lacked Weapon Specialization and Greater Weapon Focus. Restored below to the real talent,
matching how its siblings weapon-specialization-lightsabers (CR p.41) and
greater-weapon-focus-lightsabers already read.
Juyo, Tràkata and Vaapad named the generic Weapon Specialization the same way, so the
lightsaber forms were shut too. They now name the lightsaber talent.
The Elite Trooper chain is not for lightsabers — that is what the Duelist tree is for.
Greater Weapon Specialization already listed the five groups without lightsabers, but its
tree-mate Greater Weapon Focus offered all seven, so an Elite Trooper could focus in
lightsabers and then never specialize. Both now offer the same five.
The Soldier's Weapon Specialization is deliberately left alone: it names no groups, only
any exotic weapon or group you are proficient with, so lightsabers belong on its list and
proficiency does the gating. Do not restrict it to match the Weapon Master five.
_comment_chosen_weapon: Critical Strike and Halt both say 'Weapon Focus (Chosen Weapon)', which the import read as
a matchingSpec requirement — Weapon Focus held with the very group being chosen. Neither
was given a specType, so there was never a group to match against and the check read
`!!spec && ...` with spec forever undefined: both feats were unselectable no matter what
the character had. They were the only two features in the data with a matchingSpec
requirement and no choice to satisfy it, and a test asserts that stays true, since a
re-import writes the pair again from the same wording.
Neither feat is actually tied to one group. Both effects use the same wording — Critical
Strike works 'while wielding a weapon for which you possess the Weapon Focus feat', and
Halt 'if you hit with an Attack of Opportunity, while wielding a weapon for which you
possess the Weapon Focus Feat'. That is every such weapon, not one chosen when the feat is
taken. So the requirement is simply Weapon Focus with no specialization named: hasFeature
matches any spec when none is given. One feat, no choice to make, and it covers each group
you have Focus in, including ones you focus in later.
The rest of each requirements block is repeated here because the supplement merge is a
shallow spread — naming `requirements` replaces the whole block, not just the one entry.
_comment_feat_prerequisites: A sweep of every feat's `requirements` against the prerequisite line the books give it.
The two disagree in fourteen places, and where they do the block is the one that is wrong:
`prerequisites` is quoted from the source, while `requirements` is parsed out of the
spreadsheet column by tools-import-excel.mjs and can pick up the wrong number, the wrong
ability, or a token belonging to the row above.
Blocks a legal character — the feat is greyed out for someone who qualifies:
savage-attack        required Vehicular Combat, which appears nowhere in the feat. Its
line is 'Double Attack (Chosen Weapon)' and its effect is 'one
weapon group or Exotic Weapon you have selected for the Double
Attack Feat', so the requirement is Double Attack held with the very
group being chosen — exactly how its sibling Triple Attack reads.
matchingWeaponGroupProficiency goes with it: Double Attack already
demands proficiency, and applied here it would also refuse the
Exotic Weapon case the effect names outright.
autofire-assault     both read 'Weapon Focus (Chosen Weapon)' and both were parsed as a
autofire-sweep       matchingWeaponGroupProficiency with no specType to satisfy it, so
the check was `!!spec && ...` with spec forever undefined and
neither feat could be taken by anybody. Same wording, same effect
('a weapon for which you possess the Weapon Focus Feat') and so the
same fix as critical-strike and halt above: Weapon Focus, no spec.
droidcraft           required Tech Specialist. Its own description quotes the line, and
it is 'Trained in Mechanics' and nothing else. Tech Specialist
belongs to vehicle-systems-expertise, whose line does name it.
angled-throw         asked for Strength 13 where the book says Dexterity 13 — a feat
about bouncing a grenade off a wall.
bantha-herder        all four say 'Base Attack Bonus +1' and all four were given +6.
gunnery-specialist   rancor-crush's own description quotes its line in full, and it
strafe               agrees with the prerequisite field against the block.
rancor-crush
Wrong skill, which blocks and admits the wrong people at once:
deadly-sniper        'Trained in Stealth'   was checked as Acrobatics
duck-and-cover       'Trained in Stealth'   was checked as Acrobatics
deceptive-drop       'Trained in Initiative' was checked as Acrobatics
vehicle-systems-expertise  'Trained in Mechanics' was checked as Pilot
Restriction present but never actually applied:
slammer              size 'small' against a ladder spelled 'Small', so indexOf gave -1
tool-frenzy          and the comparison passed for every size including Fine. Both mean
'Small size or larger'; powerful-charge already reads 'Medium'.
Their patch carries the appendage requirement as well and lives
with the droid hardware below — one entry per feat, since a
second entry for the same id would silently win over this one.
improved-sleight-of-hand  Dexterity 13 where the book says 15.
improved-bantha-rush      lost the 'Base Attack Bonus +1' its description still quotes.
Not checked at all, though the line is a plain feat, skill or ability name the schema
already expresses. These were reaching the UI as 'not enforced automatically', which is
the right treatment for 'proficient with weapon' or 'Receive the Gamemaster's Approval'
but not for these:
droid-hunter, unstoppable-force                    'Combat Reflexes'
fight-through-pain, officer-candidacy-training,    'Force Sensitivity, Trained in Use
rapid-reaction, recovering-surge                    the Force'
unwavering-resolve                                 'Trained in Perception'
power-blast                                        'Dex 13'
staggering-attack                                  'Sneak Attack or Rapid Shot or
Rapid Strike'
The rest of the unparsed set is left alone deliberately. 'Trained in at least one
Knowledge Skill' (recall) has no way to say 'any of these' in the schema, and 'Cannot be
a Droid' (instinctive-attack, instinctive-defense) has no way to say 'not'. Showing those
beats guessing at them.
The rest of each block is restated because the merge is a shallow spread — naming
`requirements` replaces all of it, not the one entry being corrected.
_comment_unobtainable_prerequisites: A prerequisite naming a feature nothing can ever grant is a locked door. Four ids were
in that state; three are fixed here and the fourth is left standing on purpose.
droid   The Droid trait gates fourteen features — Aiming Accuracy, Damage Conversion,
Distracting Droid, Droid Shield Mastery, Erratic Target, Logic Upgrade (Skill
Swap), Mechanical Martial Arts, Multi-Targeting, Pincer, Pinpoint Accuracy,
Sensor Link, Slammer, Tool Frenzy and Turn and Burn — and no droid had it. The
Droid species entry carries no traits, because a droid is built from a degree,
a size and systems rather than a fixed stat block, so `species.features` was
left empty and the trait was never granted to anybody. It is granted below.
`species` is merged over the generated species the same way features are; that
path was added for this, since species.json is rewritten by the importer.
Granting the trait is only half of it. Seven of those fourteen lines carry a
second condition about the chassis — '2+ Appendages', '2+ Tool Appendages',
'Claw or Hand Appendage', 'Hovering or Flying Locomotion', 'Hovering, Flying,
Wheeled, or Tracked Locomotion', 'Basic Processor', 'Shield Generator' — and
none of it was checked. Unlocking the trait on its own would have handed a
walking droid with no arms the Slammer feat, which is 'you slam a target with
your appendages'. Six are now checked through `requirements.droidSystems`,
against the systems fitted in the Droid panel.
Droid Shield Mastery is the seventh and is NOT checked: it wants a Shield
Generator, and the systems catalogue has no such entry — the nearest are the
Shield Expansion Module and the Micro Shield, and neither is the thing named.
Guessing at one would refuse a legal droid, so it carries the phrase in
`unparsedPrerequisites` and the UI says it is not enforced automatically.
duros   Spacer's Surge reads 'Duros', which is a species and not a trait. The
provenance note above records 49 such prerequisites already retargeted from
features to species; this one was missed.
skill-focus-initiative   Surprisingly Quick reads 'Skill Focus (Initiative)'. The id it
named is a summary-only stub trait ('Species trait. See your sourcebook'), not
the Skill Focus feat, so holding the feat never satisfied it. It is the feat
with the Initiative specialization.
intercept-starship-maneuver   NOT fixed. Telekinetic Vigilance (Zeison Sha Warrior)
requires the Intercept starship maneuver, and that requirement is correct. The
app carries all 27 maneuvers and has a slot kind, a picker filter and a derived
`starshipManeuvers` list for them, but nothing ever builds a maneuver slot — no
class offers the choice and Starship Tactics does not grant it — so no character
can hold one. Weakening the talent would be inventing a rule to paper over a
missing feature; the fix is to grant the slots.
_comment_exotic_weapons: Exotic Weapon Proficiency is 'Choose a single Exotic Weapon', but it was imported as a
weapon-*group* choice whose allowedSpecs were five weapon ids. Nothing resolves a weapon
id against the group table, so the picker listed the five as the raw slugs 'atlatl',
'amphistaff', 'bowcaster', 'cesta' and 'flamethrower' — and the other 28 exotic weapons
in the data could not be chosen at all.
The specialization is a weapon, so specType is 'weapon'. `specWeaponGroup` narrows the
list to the exotic group rather than naming the weapons here, so a re-import that adds an
exotic weapon puts it on offer without this file being touched. The spec values are
unchanged — weapon ids, which is what prereqs.ts already looks for when it checks
matchingWeaponProficiency against exotic-weapon-proficiency — so saved characters keep
_comment_stolen_form: Stolen Form hands over the talent it names, and nothing in the data said so. The talent
reads: 'Choose one Talent from the Lightsaber Forms Talent Tree; you gain the benefits of
this Talent and are considered to have this Talent for the purpose of satisfying
prerequisites.' Held only as stolen-form(ataru), no rule keyed on the form's own id could
fire — Ataru's Dexterity-for-Strength damage silently did nothing, and a later talent
wanting Juyo did not see it either.
`specGrants` says the chosen option is gained in its own right, and the engine adds it to
the resolved feature list. It is deliberately not set on the other ten features that
choose a feature: Force Power Mastery, Force Power Adept, Force Exertion, Focused Force
Talisman, Many Shades of the Force, Share Talent, Share Force Secret, Share Force
Technique, Coordinated Leadership and Squadron Maneuvers all qualify a power or talent you
already possess rather than granting one, and expanding those would hand out a second copy.

greater-weapon-specialization-lightsaber.name: Greater Weapon Specialization (lightsabers)
description: You gain a +2 bonus on melee damage rolls with Lightsabers. This bonus stacks with the bonus granted by the Weapon Specialization (Lightsabers) talent.
greater-weapon-specialization-lightsaber.prerequisites: Greater Weapon Focus (lightsabers), Weapon Focus (lightsabers) feat, Weapon Specialization (lightsabers).

attack-combo-fire-strike.hiddenReason: the same feat as Attack Combo (Fire and Strike), which has the full text

_comment_feat_combos: Combined Feats — the Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide's term for a pair of
feats that does something extra for anyone holding both. They are not feats: nothing is
chosen and no slot is spent, and the benefit stops the moment either half is changed away.
The compendium already carries each one's wording inside the description of the feats it
belongs to, under 'Additional <Feat> Effects', which is where combos.json copies it from.
The summary spreadsheets file each pair twice, once under each half, and each row names
only the *other* feat as its prerequisite. Imported as written they became twelve
selectable feats — two per pair — each costing a slot and each demanding half of what it
should: Dodge + Running Attack could be taken by anyone with Running Attack and no Dodge
at all. All twelve are hidden here, and the pairs are written out once each in combos.json,
where both halves are named and the engine turns them on by itself. There are eight, not
six: Cleave + Follow Through and Combat Reflexes + Return Fire state their effect in the
feats' own text but were in none of the spreadsheet rows, so they had no entry at all.
Only `hidden` is set, so the merge's shallow spread leaves the rest of each row alone. A
character saved before this keeps the row it picked — hiding only governs what the pickers
offer from now on — and it reads as unsupported rather than vanishing.
attack-combo-fire-strike is a different problem with the same smell. It is the Legacy Era
feat Attack Combo (Fire and Strike), which IS a real feat with a real slot cost, arriving
a second time from the spreadsheets under an '&' spelling. The dedupe pass compares names
after punctuation is stripped but not '&' against 'and', and compares rules text, which
differs between a summary and the full entry — so the two never grouped. The summary stub
is hidden and Soldier's bonus feat list, which pointed at the stub, is pointed at the full
entry below. Its prerequisites are the same either way and the test on the '&' shorthand
still reads the stub, which is kept in the data rather than deleted.
_comment_mortar: Galaxy at War p.40 gives the Mortar Launcher four shells, and the Foundry entry for the
launcher even cross-references them — its seeAlso says "Mortar Shells". The shells
themselves are in none of the packs, so they are typed in here from
The launcher's own damage type is corrected to varies. Upstream says Slashing, which
cannot be right for a weapon that fires whatever shell you load — the same pack uses
Varies for the Espo Mortar and for the grenade launchers.
No size is given for a shell in the source, so none is set here rather than invented: size
is what decides whether a weapon needs two hands or counts as light.
Damage types follow the shell table's own TYPE column, which reads Energy for the frag
shell where the hand grenade of the same name is Slashing.
_comment_damage_gaps: Three weapons the compendium gives no damage attribute for, whose damage was only ever in
their prose. The recovered descriptions already carry the conditions — the Stokhli's
webbing acting as a Net, the Amphistaff's three forms — so only the numbers are added.
The stun flag is deliberately not set on these two. It renders as "stun setting" and
"Can be set to stun", which describes a blaster you can switch; these deal stun and
nothing else, so it is written into the damage line instead. damageType is nulled where
the line already names the types, so the label does not append a second one.
_comment_stun: Stun settings, harvested from swse.fandom.com — one page per weapon, since the batch API
silently truncates the later pages, and folding non-breaking spaces first because the
field is written 'Stun Setting:' with one. Of 245 weapons, 149 name a setting and 91 say
Ten weapons deal stun and nothing else and had no damage at all; their dice are written
into the damage line, as the Stokhli and Neuronic Whip already were, so no stun flag,
which would wrongly imply something switchable.
Forty-two can be switched between normal and stun as a Swift Action, so they carry
stun: true. Six of those hit harder on stun and carry stunDamage as well; the rest use
The ammunition-fed launchers are deliberately not flagged. Their stun line reads Varies,
meaning it depends which shell is loaded, not that the launcher itself has a setting.

mortar-frag.name: Mortar, Frag
mortar-frag.notes: A shell for the Mortar Launcher. Fin-stabilised and self-guiding, with targeting sensors and a high-yield warhead; it lands two rounds after firing and covers a 2x2 square area. Availability: Military.

mortar-ion.name: Mortar, Ion
mortar-ion.notes: A shell for the Mortar Launcher, dealing ion damage against droids and vehicles. Lands two rounds after firing and covers a 2x2 square area. Availability: Military.

mortar-stun.name: Mortar, Stun
mortar-stun.notes: A shell for the Mortar Launcher, dealing stun damage. Lands two rounds after firing and covers a 2x2 square area. Availability: Military.

mortar-thermal.name: Mortar, Thermal
mortar-thermal.notes: The heaviest shell for the Mortar Launcher. Lands two rounds after firing and covers a 4x4 square area. Availability: Military.
